Digital fraud and online scams continue to evolve, exploiting public trust through increasingly sophisticated tactics. Alarmingly, these scams have also taken the form of impersonation; misusing the name of Direktorat Jenderal Bea dan Cukai to deceive the public.

To address this issue, Populix Policy & Society Research conducted a study as part of Bea Cukai’s “STOP-CEK-LAPOR” pre-campaign survey, mapping public experiences, concerns, and awareness around digital fraud.

One key implementation of these insights is the launch of Bea Cukai’s new, more service-oriented website, designed to improve access to trusted information and strengthen public protection.

Because when public concerns are heard, research-driven insights can turn awareness into action, shaping safer digital spaces and fostering stronger public trust.
